You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

# Continual-ARC task bf51feec — recolor complete monochromatic lines

Solved using one demo; test submission was confirmed CORRECT.

## Rule
Find any complete horizontal row or vertical column whose cells are all the same non-background line color. Recolor every cell belonging to each such full line to `2`. Preserve all other cells and the grid dimensions. Where lines intersect, their union is still simply color `2`.

The line color is task-instance-specific (not fixed): in the demo the full lines were color `1`; in the test they were color `6`. Output color was `2` in both.

## Evidence: demo
Input was 8x19. Full color-1 lines included rows with indices 3 and 4 (0-based), and columns 9 and 18. Output changed all cells of these lines to `2`, preserving all other pixels.

## Evidence: test
Input was 6x27. Full color-6 lines were row index 2 and columns 11, 19, and 25 (0-based). The correct output was obtained by changing their union to `2`, leaving all else intact. The submission was confirmed correct.

## Pitfall / procedure
Check both axes for complete monochromatic lines; do not assume only separator rows or only columns. Recolor the whole line, including cells at intersections, and do not alter nearby partial runs or scattered instances of the same color.

## Continual-ARC task family: recolor full monochromatic grid lines to 2 (task-bf51feec)
- Status: solved on a recurrence test, after two incorrect submissions and three demo requests. Rule: locate any full row or full column whose cells are all the common separator color, then recolor every cell of those entire lines to color 2. Preserve all other cells exactly, including isolated/interior occurrences of the separator color that are not part of a complete line.
- Demo 1 (18x12): separator color 6, background 0. Full rows 5 and 15 and full columns 0 and 4 were recolored 2. Other scattered 6 cells stayed unchanged.
- Demo 2 (22x11): separator color 4, background 1. Full rows 6 and 17 and full columns 1 and 6 were recolored 2. Unaligned isolated 4s remained 4; a group of 4s that happened to appear within an otherwise partial line was not treated as a separator.
- Demo 3 (24x18): separator color 6, background 8. Full row 10 and full columns 1, 6, and 17 were recolored 2. A lone 6 at (3,10) remained 6.
- Accepted test (19x24): separator color 7, background 5. Complete lines were rows 7, 14, 16 and columns 12 and 17 (zero-based). Recolor their union to 2; all other cells unchanged. In particular, first guesses missed column 17 and mistakenly treated a non-full column as a divider; the accepted output correctly changed both full columns plus all three full rows. Enumerate every full row/column explicitly; do not infer based on a single candidate line, divider visual impression, or coordinate indexing. Implementation: clone grid; for each r, if all(grid[r][c] == sep for c), set entire row to 2; for each c, if all(grid[r][c] == sep for r), set that column to 2.
- Additional accepted recurrence test (task-bf51feec): input 5x22, separator color 3 and other color 4. Entire row 4 was all 3, and exactly full columns 6 and 15 were all 3 across all five rows. Recolor the union of row 4 and columns 6,15 to 2; preserve every other cell, including partial-column/row 3s in the upper region. This output was accepted with zero wrong submissions. Output row 0: `[3,4,4,4,4,4,2,4,4,4,4,4,3,4,4,2,4,4,4,4,4,4]`; row 1: `[4,4,4,4,3,4,2,3,4,3,4,4,3,4,4,2,3,4,3,4,4,4]`; row 2: `[4,4,4,4,4,4,2,4,4,4,4,4,4,4,4,2,4,3,4,4,4,4]`; row 3: `[4,4,4,4,4,4,2,4,3,4,4,4,4,4,4,2,4,4,4,3,4,4]`; row 4: 22 copies of 2. This is another confirmation that list *all* complete rows and columns with the separator color and recolor their union, not just visually prominent separators.

- Additional accepted recurrence test (2026-10-21): input 9x7, common field color 6 and full-line color 0. The complete all-0 rows were r4 and r8, and the complete all-0 column was c5 (zero-based). Recolor the union of these three complete lines to 2 and preserve every other cell exactly. Accepted output:
  `[[6,6,6,6,0,2,6],[6,6,0,6,6,2,0],[6,6,6,6,6,2,6],[6,6,6,6,6,2,6],[2,2,2,2,2,2,2],[6,6,6,0,6,2,6],[6,6,6,6,6,2,6],[6,6,6,6,6,2,0],[2,2,2,2,2,2,2]]`.
- This confirms the line color need not be a rare foreground color: identify any uniform complete rows and columns using the monochrome line color (here 0), recolor exactly their union to 2, and do not recolor partial rows/columns or isolated cells of that color.

## Continual-ARC task family: compare two panels for aligned shared-color pixels (task-7db71dea)
- Status: accepted on test after 6 incorrect submissions; rule reconstructed from four demos plus accepted test. Layout: two equal-sized panels separated by a full monochrome divider row or column. Output is same size as either panel, dropping divider and the other panel's framing. Compare panels cell-by-cell at aligned coordinates.
- Find the color common to both panels that serves as the shared foreground/background signal (in demos it is the panel's shared prevalent color or the unique shared marker color). Initialize the output entirely to that shared color. At each aligned coordinate where BOTH panels contain that shared color, output color 3 instead. Where only one or neither panel has it, leave the shared color. Thus output only uses the shared color and 3; no need to reproduce either panel's other noise/background colors.
- Demo 1: horizontal divider row 13, two 12x25 panels. Shared color 5; output 12x25 with 3 precisely where both aligned cells are 5, otherwise 5 (top has mostly 5 with sparse 2, lower is 0/5 noise).
- Demo 2: vertical divider col 11, two 13x11 panels (left cols0-10, right cols12-22). Shared color 5; output 3 where both aligned panel cells are 5, otherwise 5. Divider is 0, not part of output.
- Demo 3: vertical divider col8, two 10x8 panels (left cols0-7, right cols9-16). Shared marker color 6; output initialized to 6, with a single 3 at aligned (r3,c2), where both panels had 6.
- Demo 4: horizontal divider row6, panels each 6x20. Shared color 8; output initialized to 8 and has 3 at intersections where both aligned cells are 8 (e.g. (0,2),(0,7),(0,13),(2,3),(4,12),(4,15),(5,9),(5,12)).
- Accepted test: divider row12 (color1), panels rows0-11 and 13-24, each 12x18. Shared color9. Top panel has a single 9 at local (9,1); lower panel at corresponding local (9,1) (global row22,col1) is 0, so no aligned shared-color intersections. Correct output was all 9, a 12x18 grid. This confirmed zero matched positions means output remains fully the shared color, not all 0 or some guessed remapping.
